title: OLTP vs OLAP
description: Why transactional systems store data by row, analytical systems store it by column, and the two workloads end up on separate infrastructure.
beats: OLTP runs the business, a few rows at a time
OLAP answers questions about the business
The shapes conflict, so the systems split

title: The Data Warehouse
description: The warehouse gave analytics governed, modeled, ACID-backed tables. Its limits are format lock-in, structured data only, and a cost curve tied to one vendor's engine.
beats: One governed place to ask questions
Structured data only, in someone else's format
Storage, compute and format bound together

title: The Evolution to the Data Lakehouse
description: Warehouse, then data lake, then lakehouse: the path from a closed governed store to open files on object storage that behave like real tables.
beats: The warehouse: reliable, closed, expensive
The data lake: open and cheap, but not a table
A table format turns files into a table
Warehouse behaviour on storage you own

title: Data Lakes and Apache Parquet
description: Object storage is the cheap open substrate; Apache Parquet is the columnar file format — column chunks, encodings and footer statistics — that makes scanning it fast.
beats: Object storage is cheap, durable and open
Parquet stores data by column, not by row
Footer statistics let engines skip data

title: Open Table Formats
description: A table format is the metadata layer that turns a directory of Parquet into a real table — and the three open ones each solve it a little differently.
beats: A directory of Parquet is not a table
Metadata names the exact set of files
Database guarantees on open files
Same problem, three designs

title: Catalogs and Apache Polaris
description: A catalog holds the current pointer for every table and makes commits atomic. Apache Polaris is an open-source, vendor-neutral implementation of the Iceberg REST Catalog spec.
beats: A catalog is the table's source of truth
The Iceberg REST Catalog is an open API
An open-source Iceberg REST catalog

title: The Lakehouse and Agentic AI
description: Agents query data without an analyst in the loop, which moves access control, definitions and auditability down to the table and the catalog.
beats: Agents query data on their own
Permissions have to hold at the table
One copy, many engines, one meaning
Agents need context, not just access

title: Semantic Layers
description: A semantic layer holds the endorsed metrics, dimensions and joins every consumer resolves against. Apache Ossie (incubating) is the open standard for moving those definitions between tools.
beats: Every tool redefines the same metric
One governed place for meaning
Definitions written in one vendor's dialect
An open standard for semantic interchange

title: What Is Apache Arrow?
description: Arrow is the in-memory counterpart to Parquet: one agreed columnar layout so systems can hand data to each other with no serialization step at all.
beats: Every hop used to re-encode the data
One columnar layout, agreed in advance
Zero-copy interchange, vectorized execution
